newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market ends quiet ahead of auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market ends quiet ahead of auction.

text.p: Prices of government securities moved up in dull trade while overnight money was inactive on the reporting Friday, dealers said.
Banks do not borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Dealers said trade in securities was also dull as the market awaits results of the 14-day repos auction which the Reserve Bank of India holds later on Friday.
Dealers said they expected the auction cut-off to be between five and six percent.
"It is unlikely to be higher as the 91-day treasury bill cut-off is 6.94 percent," a dealer at a state-run bank said.

He said the auction cut-off would determine the call money rates for the next fortnight. "I do not see call money higher than seven percent during next fortnight. More funds are being released through the CRR cut tomorrow," he said.
A half-percentage point cut in banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirements takes place on Saturday, releasing over 21 billion rupees to banks.
The reversal of a four-day repos held earlier in the week by the RBI would also release over nine billion rupees to banks.
"All this liquidity should keep call rates in control," the dealer said.
Dealers said the 13.50 percent 1997 government stock was traded at a yield of 10.11 percent against a last traded price of 10.42 percent.
The 364-day treasury bill auctioned on Wednesday at 10.12 percent was traded on Friday at 9.90 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said there were no trades in certificates of deposit and commercial paper.
